title: {{name}} and the Big Crab
back_blurb: When {{other}} takes {{name}}'s ball, {{name}} goes quiet and tells no one.
But on a magic beach, a big crab is taking everyone's shells.
Can {{name}} find a strong voice, and the Lifeguard Whistle, before the water comes in?

text: It was a sunny day at the club in {{place}}. {{name}}, {{age}}, had a new ball.
Then {{other}} grabbed it. "Ha! Baby can't catch it!"
Other kids laughed too. {{name}}'s band went grey.
{{name}} did not say a word. {{He}} went home and shut the door.
{{He}} did not tell anyone.

options.label: No
options.response: That's right. When someone is mean, it is never your fault.

options.label: Yes
options.response: No! {{other}} was mean. {{name}} did nothing wrong.

text: Then {{sidekick}}'s eyes lit up, and the big seashell began to hum.
{{name}} held it to {{his}} ear. Whoosh! The sea pulled {{him}} in.
pages.sign: A sign said: Snap hid the Lifeguard Whistle. The water is coming in!

text: {{His}} band had a tiny screen.
{{name}} stood tall. "I am here!" A shiny bubble shield popped up around {{him}}.
pages.screen: STRONG VOICE = SHIELD UP · HIDING = SHIELD DOWN

challenge.question: What makes the shield come up?

options.label: A strong voice
options.response: Yes! Stand tall, speak loud, shield up.

options.label: Hiding
options.response: Hiding makes the shield go down. Try again.

text: Little crabs were stuck behind a big rock.
"Can I help?" {{name}} said in a strong voice.
Bump, bump, BUMP! {{His}} shield pushed the rock away.
A tiny hermit crab was crying. She had no shell.
"I'm Lulu. Snap took my shell, and he hid the whistle so no one can call Teta Turtle."

challenge.question: Look at the sand. Which way did Snap go?

options.label: The big claw marks
options.response: Yes! Big crab, big marks. Let's go!

options.label: The little footprints
options.response: Those are too small for Snap. Try again.

text: A seagull grabbed {{name}}'s snack. "Ha ha! Too slow!"
"Stinky bird!" {{name}} shouted, and {{his}} shield went down.
Then {{he}} stood tall. "Stop. I don't like that." And {{he}} walked away.
In the sand was a shell with words on it. "Read it, quick!" said {{sidekick}}.

challenge.question: Help {{name}} read the riddle.
riddle: When someone is mean, I am the thing to do.
I am not a tattle. I keep you safe too. What am I?

options.label: Telling a grown-up
options.response: Telling! {{name}} kept the riddle in {{his}} pocket.

options.label: Being mean back
options.response: That makes things worse. Try again.

options.label: Keeping it secret
options.response: Secrets keep you alone. Try again.

text: There was Snap, the biggest crab, on a pile of shells.
Next to him was the Lifeguard Whistle! "Mine, mine, all mine!"
But look. Snap had a little band too.
Snap ran into a cave. "You can't find me!"
{{name}} took one slow breath. "I will find the whistle. Then I will tell."

challenge.question: Trace the tunnels with your finger. Which one leads to the whistle?

options.label: Blue shells
options.response: The blue tunnel! There's the whistle.

text: Snap grabbed {{sidekick}} with his big claw. "Ha! Tiny baby!"
{{name}} froze. {{His}} shield went down.
The water rushed in, up to {{his}} knees!
"I won't hide this time," said {{name}}.
{{He}} remembered {{his}} Power Word. And {{he}} needed your help.

challenge.question: Stand up and do each step:
steps: **Breathe.** In, then slowly out. Three times.
**Stand tall and say it loud:** "Stop. I don't like that."
challenge.done: {{His}} shield came up, bigger and shinier than ever!

text: "STOP. I don't like that!" said {{name}}, loud and strong. Snap let {{sidekick}} go.
{{name}} grabbed the whistle and blew. Tweeeet!
Teta Turtle swam in fast. "Thank you for telling me," she said, and pushed the water back.
"Nobody plays with me," Snap said quietly. "So I take things."
"Taking is not OK," said Teta Turtle. Snap gave back the shells. "Sorry."

challenge.question: Who can you tell when someone is mean? Tick every one.

options.label: A seagull
options.response: Ha! No. Tell a big person.

challenge.done: Yes! There are lots of big people who can help.

text: Back at the club, {{other}} grabbed the ball again. "Baby!"
{{name}} hugged {{his}} tummy and took three breaths. "{{power_word}}"
{{He}} stood tall. "Stop. I don't like that." Then {{he}} told Mama. "Can you help me?"
Mama helped, and the ball came back. {{sidekick}} winked. "Best {{strength}} in {{place}}."
